newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: PLDT FALLS ON OVERSEAS PHONE CHARGE CUTS.
newsitem.headline: PLDT FALLS ON OVERSEAS PHONE CHARGE CUTS.

text.p: Philippine Long Distance Telephone Co shares fell 35 pesos, or 3.89 percent, to 865 pesos in early trading on Tuesday following the sharp overnight drop of its American Depositary Receipt (ADR), traders said.

Brokers said PLDT shares continued to be hounded by news late last week that the U.S. Federal Communications Commission approved rules that would slash the price of overseas phone calls by an average price of 20 cents a minute from the present 88 cents over five years.
PLDT's ADR fell $1 7/16 on Monday to close at $30 9/16.
PLDT was the most actively traded issue in early trade with turnover at 130.76 million pesos.
It reached an intra-day low of 845 pesos.

"PLDT is down and it's still on sentiment that the accounting rate will be slashed and yet there is still no sign whether it's proposed rebalancing of rates will be approved," said Ramon Saulo, senior investment analyst at Asiamerit Securities.
Revenues from international calls make up about 50 percent of PLDT's revenues.

To make up for the proposed cut in the accounting rate, which is the charge per minute of processed international calls, PLDT asked the government to allow a restructuring of its rates that would raise basic phone charges and implement a call metering scheme.
The National Telecommunications Commission has yet to act on PLDT's application.
